summary: Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris, Sorbonne, and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She served as directeur d’études at EPHE (1938–1963).

Marco Ferrante specializes in Indology and philosophy, earning his BA and PhD at Sapienza University of Rome. He held positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2018, 2020–2025), Oxford (2018–2020), and the University of Vienna (2017–2025).

Marco Franceschini is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Turin. He served at the University of Bologna as assistant professor (attested 2019) and became associate professor in 2021.

Marco Trombetta works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at Seoul National University (2009–2023) and held a post at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
Marco Walther is a Tibetologist who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marco della Tomba was an Indology and religious studies scholar and missionary. He served in the Tibet-Hindustan Mission (1757–1773) and later held the roles of propraefectus (1786) and praefectus (1801) in the Tibet Mission.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Nagoya University, Heidelberg, and Würzburg (PhD ~2001–2004). He held posts at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marcus Joseph Müller studied at Munich, Leiden, and Paris, working in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor of non-biblical Oriental literature at the University of Munich from 1840 until at least 1847.

Marek Mejor is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied at the University of Warsaw under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and later served as professor at the University of Warsaw.
Marek Zemánek specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, completing his dissertation under Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Sheffield (~1972–1976) and later held an academic post there (~1981–2011).
Margaret Cone is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who held affiliations at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (both attested 1996).
Margaret Elizabeth Noble was a religious studies and Indology scholar. She attended Halifax Ladies' College and studied under Swami Vivekananda beginning in 1898.
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish studied at Yale, USC, and Claremont Graduate University. Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, she served as an associate professor of religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. Her major posts included positions at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), and Fordham University (1968–1970).

Margaret R. Miles, a religious studies scholar and historian, earned her PhD at the Graduate Theological Union. She held faculty appointments at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and served as dean of the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarethe Steiner was an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe in 1926. She also studied under Jakob Wilhelm Hauer and held a post at Tübingen in 1939.

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower, studied under Xiuping Hong, and held a position at the University of Pittsburgh.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Central Asian studies. She studied at St. Petersburg State University and served as a researcher and manuscript curator at the Russian Academy of Sciences.
